clue.text: Cast raising a bit of money before start of play

definitions.text: raising a bit of money before start of play

blocks.note: first meaning: throw, fling

blocks.clueFragment: raising a bit of money before start of play
blocks.note: second meaning: flipping a coin into the air before a cricket or football match begins

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like fundraising for a theatre show; the 'bit of money' is a coin flipped to decide who bats or kicks off first.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast and to toss are both synonyms for throwing, and the coin flip deciding ends or batting order is called the toss.

clue.text: Language skill not evident in two of the three R's?

definitions.text: Language skill not evident in two of the three R's?

blocks.clueFragment: Language skill not evident in two of the three R's?
blocks.note: surface reading: a skill missing from basic schooling
setter's reading: the three R's are reading, writing and arithmetic, and two of those words do not actually begin with R, so whoever named them could not get the letters right

explanation.surface: A complaint that schools neglect one language skill while teaching the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The three R's is a jokey name for reading, writing and arithmetic; only reading starts with R, so the skill absent from 'wRiting' and 'aRithmetic' is getting letters right.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the letters of words in correct order is a basic literacy ability taught at school.

clue.text: Get on front of stage, entering right

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
a letter entering a word goes in through it and ends up inside

blocks.note: proper means right, correct
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to an actor: make progress by stepping forward on the right side of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of stage' looks like theatre jargon, but it only means the first letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on in life is an idiom for doing well and thriving, just as to prosper is.

clue.text: One in herd attracted by female, with yen for cow

blocks.clueFragment: One in herd attracted by female
blocks.note: the male of the cattle herd, drawn to the cows
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of a male beast drawn to a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' at the end looks like the animal, but it is a verb here: to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, which is what a bully does to victims.

clue.text: Friendship that's unusually dear in America, oddly

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from its normal order, so these letters get rearranged
acting oddly means behaving strangely, so the following place name is jumbled too
one word sits in the other, so the first group is placed inside the second

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that friendship costs a surprising amount in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work separately here: each word is jumbled on its own before one goes inside the other, which is why 'in' sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is the warm comradeship and mutual trust among companions, a close synonym.

clue.text: Lovers disturbed someone like you

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A couple interrupted in a tender moment by an intruder like the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The reader of the clue is busy cracking the puzzle, so a person like you is one who works out crosswords.

clue.text: Doctor Who adds this sort of novelty, at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each following word

blocks.clueFragment: Who adds this sort of novelty
blocks.note: initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A comment on the TV series Doctor Who bringing something new to the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like one title, but the Doctor is the definition and 'Who' starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr John Watson is the medical man who narrates and assists in the Sherlock Holmes stories.

clue.text: Weapon for shooting jets

blocks.note: surface reading: an anti-aircraft gun for bringing down jet planes
setter's reading: a toy that squirts streams of liquid

explanation.surface: Military hardware designed to bring down fast aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jets' suggests fighter planes; here they are spurts of water fired from a children's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy gun squirts streams of liquid when its trigger is pulled, so it literally fires jets.

clue.text: Outstanding victory eclipsed by defensive disaster, in short

indicators.note: something eclipsed is covered over by another body, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: OG is the short form of own goal, a defender's blunder in football
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A football report: a great win overshadowed by a calamitous defensive error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the victory, but it means unpaid. An own goal is when a player knocks the ball into their own net.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding remains unpaid, and money still due is owing.

clue.text: Doing wrong part of test, taking last piece first

indicators.note: the final letter is brought round to the front of the word

blocks.note: a cricket Test match is divided into innings

explanation.surface: Cheating in an exam by grabbing the last question first.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; each team's turn at batting is an innings. Move its final S to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinning means committing a wrong against moral or religious law, so it is doing wrong.

clue.text: Person keeping an eye on love poetry by monarch

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
verse is poetry
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone supervising romantic poems written by a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor watches over workers or a process, which is what someone keeping an eye on things does.

clue.text: Uniform for lieutenant as tailored initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A military outfit made to measure for a junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' sits with lieutenant and tailored to suggest army dress, but it is an adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform surface is level and even throughout, without bumps, which is what flat describes.

clue.text: Characters on pitch showing little variation as players

blocks.note: type is printed characters
on joins the two halves, one placed after the other
to pitch is to throw, or cast

explanation.surface: Players on a sports pitch whose personalities barely differ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters', 'pitch' and 'players' all suggest a sports field, but the answer is about actors stuck in one kind of role.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who are always given the same kind of role show little range across their performances.

clue.text: Part in Tempest or Macbeth? The former

indicators.note: a part in the following words means a stretch of letters inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first title and the start of 'or'

explanation.surface: A question about casting an actor in one of two Shakespeare plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests an acting role. 'The former' refers back to Tempest, the first of the two plays named.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent gale with heavy rain, so the former of the two words means the same.

clue.text: Send up wages divided by staff

indicators.note: something divided by another has that other running through its middle

blocks.note: pay is wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Mocking how payroll is split among employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something up is a British idiom for mocking it by imitation, which is what a spoof does.

clue.text: Man on board interrupting African opposed to government

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something else

blocks.note: a person from Liberia in West Africa
a tar is a sailor, a man on board ship

explanation.surface: A man at a board meeting cutting in on an African delegate who rejects the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' hints at a committee, but it means aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertarian believes in individual freedom and wants the state's role kept minimal or removed.

clue.text: Complaint I will put before head

blocks.note: contracted to I'll
places the first part ahead of the second
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will take their grievance to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance and 'head' as a boss; a ness is a coastal promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean a medical disorder or ailment, as in a chest complaint.

clue.text: Men's appearance in sound only

indicators.note: only in sound means the word matches when spoken, not when spelt

blocks.note: guise means outward appearance

explanation.surface: A remark that men's looks are a matter of hearing, not sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Men is', the definition followed by a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Guys is informal everyday slang for males, chiefly fellows or blokes.

clue.text: Relative amounts misrepresented in centre pages

indicators.note: something misrepresented is given a false form, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Statistics distorted in a newspaper's middle spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion out of a hundred expresses one quantity in relation to a whole, which is a relative amount.

clue.text: Running the kind of movie that's highly entertaining?

definitions.text: the kind of movie that's highly entertaining?

blocks.note: first meaning: fleeing, escaping

blocks.clueFragment: the kind of movie that's highly entertaining?
blocks.note: second meaning: a film shown on an aircraft, entertaining passengers high in the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly entertaining' sounds like great praise; it literally means entertainment at altitude. Running here means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives are said to be in flight when escaping, and airline films are screened during a flight.

clue.text: Crooked fellow, one to be put inside?

definitions.text: Crooked fellow, one to be put inside?

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order
put inside says one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dishonest man who deserves to be locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a criminal heading for jail while also giving the wordplay; 'Crooked' does double duty as part of the picture and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal or disreputable person is a lowlife, and such a crook is someone likely to be jailed.

clue.text: Nothing in ancient vessel for shipwrecked sailor

indicators.note: one thing sits in another, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: a cruse is an old earthenware jar for oil or water
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An empty old ship standing for a castaway mariner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship to fit the sailor, but it is a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Defoe's fictional castaway, marooned on a desert island after his ship was wrecked.

clue.text: Time and determination needed for woven fabric

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
joins the two parts
will is determination

explanation.surface: Weaving cloth requires patience and resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a textile woven with a diagonal ribbed pattern, such as denim or gabardine.

clue.text: Part of our capital, thus, goes on house

blocks.note: so means thus
puts the next part after the first
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A note about a London district continuing to house people.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London known for theatres, restaurants and nightlife; 'our capital' assumes a British reader.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively West End neighbourhood is one district within London, the British capital city.
